chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:
Being affectionate toward the people is half of the intellect.

key_terms.التوادد: Tawaddud — active affection and endearment, the deliberate showing of warmth and love to others
key_terms.العقل: 'Aql — the intellect or reason, the faculty of wise judgment and right action in Shia thought

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Kazim say about showing affection to people?
ai.summary: Imam al-Kazim (peace be upon him) teaches that half of a person's intellect is expressed through their warmth and affection toward others. This hadith belongs to a broader Shia ethical tradition that ties social virtue to rational excellence — true wisdom is not merely theoretical knowledge but manifests in how one treats fellow human beings. The original audience understood 'aql (intellect/reason) as the faculty that guides right action, so saying tawaddud constitutes half of it elevates social kindness to a matter of spiritual and rational priority.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Hassan, from Musa Bin Bakr, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Being affectionate towards the people is half the intellect’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Hassan from Musa ibn Bakr from abu al-Hassan (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Showing that one loves people is one half (the power) of reason.”
